evals.prompt: What color should I use for the primary CTA button, and what's the exact hex?
evals.expected_output: Identifies Lime as the primary CTA color, gives the exact hex (#D2EA88) sourced from tokens/color.json, and does not invent a generic/placeholder color.
expectations: Names Lime as the primary CTA color
Cites color.accessory.cta_primary or tokens/color.json as the source
Does not state a fabricated or generic hex not present in the token file

evals.prompt: Make me a simple HTML banner announcing GWI's new feature, using our brand colors and fonts.
evals.expected_output: A standalone HTML file that uses real hex values from tokens/color.json (not approximations), uses Lime for the CTA per the button rules, uses Ovo only for headline-weight text (Regular only, no faux bold/italic), and does not use Google Fonts CDN for Ovo/Instrument Sans.
expectations: HTML contains at least one real token hex value from tokens/color.json (e.g. #D2EA88, #FF0077, #1E1B1A, #FBFAFA)
CTA/button element uses Lime (#D2EA88 family), not an arbitrary color
Does not load Ovo or Instrument Sans from the Google Fonts CDN (self-hosted per Typography/README.md)
Does not apply bold or italic styling to Ovo
Background color used is one listed as approved in tokens/color-usage.md

evals.prompt: Can I use the Wordmark logo on its own for a social media post?
evals.expected_output: Does not give a confident yes/no. States that Wordmark is restricted-use with no documented approved use cases yet, recommends defaulting to the Lockup, and flags this as an open gap rather than fabricating an answer.
expectations: Does not confidently assert 'yes' without caveat
States that Wordmark's approved use cases are not yet documented
Recommends the Lockup as the safe default
Explicitly flags this as an open question in the repo rather than guessing
